 Appearance:
 MR. R. K. RAJPUT(6988) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR SALIM M SAIYED(5172) for the Respondent(s) No. 3  MR MEET THAKKAR, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

sentences.text: The present petition is filed by the petitioner invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India and Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
It is pertinent to note that the present petition has been filed by the petitioner on 29.10.2025 when the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code are no more in operation.
Therefore, this petition is basically filed invoking the powers of this Court under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

By filing this petition, the petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs:
"A. YOUR LORDSHIP may be pleased to ADMIT and allow this Petition.
B. YOUR LORDSHIP may be pleased to QUASH AND SET ASIDE the First Information Report bearing FIR No. 11191011250332 registered with the D.C.B.
Police Station, Ahmedabad City, for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and all NEUTRAL CITATION Ajaybhai Fakirchand Gandhi vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86049405/
1 R/SCR.A/14575/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined consequential proceedings arising therefrom, with respect to the Petitioner, Mr. Ajaybhai Fakirchand Gandhi.
C.

sentences.text:
YOUR LORDSHIP may be pleased to stay further proceedings of the impugned F.I.R. being FIR No. 11191011250332 registered with the D.C.B. Police Station,
Ahmedabad City, at Annexure 'A' and all subsequent proceedings, pending the admission, hearing and final disposal of this application;

D. YOUR LORDSHIP may be pleased to grant such other and further relief as deemed just and proper in the interest of justice"
2.

The facts and circumstances giving rise to the filing of the petition are such that an offence came to be registered with D.C.B Police Station, Ahmedabad City against the petitioner and the other co-accused under Sections 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

Being aggrieved by the said FIR,
the petitioner has approached this Court by filing the present petition.
3. Heard learned advocate Shri. R. K. Rajput appearing for the petitioner.
He submitted that the dispute involved in the present FIR is purely of a civil nature which is sought to be given a criminal color by lodging the present FIR.
He further submitted that the first informant had taken recourse to civil proceedings against the petitioner and had also filed an application for execution of a consent decree.
However, the said execution petition was dismissed by the competent Court as a petitioner herein had not signed indicating any settlement being arrived at between the first informant and himself.

Against the said order, NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/14575/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined the respondent has approached this Court by filing Special Civil Application No.15998 of 2023 which is pending before this Court and no relief whatsoever has been granted in favour of the respondent.

He further submitted that there is a gross delay in lodging the present FIR as the incident alleged in the FIR had taken place between 29.09.2011 to 30.06.2024 for which the FIR came to be lodged on 15.10.2025.
The delay caused in lodging the FIR has not been explained by the first informant.
The petitioner is aged about 73 years.
The petitioner had never approached the first informant and had not promised allotment of any property in his favour and therefore, he cannot be arraigned as an accused in the present offence.
The FIR has been lodged by the respondent with an ulterior motive after having failed to obtain a suitable order in the civil proceedings.
He therefore submitted to allow the present petition and quash and set aside the FIR in question.

4. Learned APP has opposed the present petition containing that the averments made in the FIR by the first informant clearly make out the ingredients for the offences against the petitioner and the other co-accused.
He therefore submitted to dismiss the present petition.
5. Learned Advocate Shri.
Salim M. Saiyed, appearing for the complainant, has also opposed the petition.

sentences.text: 6. Heard learned Advocate for the parties.

As per the FIR, the first informant had made some investments in one Kunj Infra Development Pvt. Ltd. and the co-accused Keyur Jitendrabhai Patel and Kiran Ramjibhai Patel were the owners of the said NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/14575/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined
Kunj Infra Development Pvt. Ltd.

Thereafter, some dispute arose between the first informant and the aforesaid co-accused and therefore, the first informant had submitted an application against them in the office of CID crime and had also instituted a Civil Suit against them in the competent Court.

The aforesaid co- accused, with an intention to get the said Civil Suit disposed of, had tried to enter into an agreement with the first informant, which was initially discarded by the first informant.

Thereafter, the other co-accused, namely Arvindbhai Jayantibhai Parikh, had intervened between the aforesaid co-accused and the first informant and thereafter, the aforesaid co-accused had informed the first informant that because of the financial difficulty, they were not in a position to complete the construction work of Kunj Grand and therefore, they had sold the entire scheme to Sevantilal Fakirchand and Co. Pvt. Ltd. and Arham Developers.

entities.text: Sevantilal Fakirchand and Co. Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner herein happens to be the owner of the Arham Developers.

It was promised to the first informant that in the scheme developed by Sevantilal Fakirchand and Co. as well as Arham Developers, 13 offices would be allotted to the first informant and therefore, the first informant had agreed to withdraw the suit filed by him.
The agreement entered into between the parties was also notarized.

However, since no offices were allotted to the first informant as agreed,
the first informant had not withdrawn the suit.

Upon being asked, the first informant was informed that since the construction work was in progress and the Building Use Permission was not granted,
the possession of the 13 offices could not be delivered to him and since some time had elapsed after the agreement was arrived between the parties, the first informant was further promised for NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/14575/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined allotment of 3 more offices.
An agreement to that effect was also executed in the year 2012.
Thereafter, the first informant withdrew the Civil Suit on the basis of the terms of agreement arrived between the parties.

In the year 2014, the possession of 16 offices was handed over to the first informant with the respective possession letters and it was promised that a saledeed in that regard would be executed in favor of the first informant after the BU permission is granted.

The first informant came to know upon inquiry that, in the interregnum, the accused persons had executed saledeeds in favor of different persons though, these offices were agreed to be allotted to the first informant.
7. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner that he had never entered into any agreement with the first informant and therefore he cannot be held liable for the offence.

However, the perusal of the FIR indicates that the petitioner herein being the owner of the Arham Developers had executed a Power of Attorney in favor of Rameshbhai Madhavbhai Shah and he was very much aware about the agreement arrived at between the parties with regard to the 16 offices.
It also appears from the record that the first informant was also issued possession letters for the 16 offices in question.
Therefore, at this stage, the involvement of the petitioner in the offence cannot be ruled out.
A detailed investigation into the offence would be required for ascertaining the involvement of the petitioner in the offence.

8. The facts narrated hereinabove, prima facie make out the intention on the part of the accused to cheat the first informant NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/14575/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined from the very inception.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to exercise discretion in favor of Ajaybhai Fakirchand Gandhi vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86049405/
